reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2, E3) supports that laser cladding can deposit a FeCrNiTiZr HEA coating with high hardness and good elevated-temperature wear resistance on H13 steel, and that laser cladding offers rapid cooling and metallurgical bonding. However, none of the cited passages provide evidence regarding the formation of a single-phase microstructure, the elimination of intergranular films, the mitigation of hot cracking, or enhanced fatigue and oxidation resistance relative to fusion-weld repairs. These key premises are therefore unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: Laser cladding produces a refined, homogeneous, single-phase microstructure in the deposited HEA coating.
This refined microstructure eliminates low-melting intergranular films that cause hot cracking.
The FeCrNiTiZr HEA coating forms a strong metallurgical bond with the substrate.
The HEA coating exhibits enhanced fatigue, wear, and oxidation resistance compared to conventional fusion-weld repairs.
The HEA coating mitigates hot cracking via multicomponent mixing during rapid solidification.
